findings.evidence: R6 and AC24 cover writes to all five blocks required by amended decision 6c, while R4(c), AC20 and AC27 make secrets and actions read-only.
R7 and AC33 require and verify publication on process readiness and subsequent module degraded/ready transitions, with AC34 checking atomic replacement.
AC38 verifies that unsaved edits change Check results in both directions while leaving overlay bytes unchanged.

R6 explicitly protects descendants during ancestor writes and removals, and AC27 tests preserved references, rejected replacements or omissions, credential-containing ancestor removal, and referenced mapping keys.
AC32 now starts with a live process and matching digest, then requires an unapplied save that changes the effective configuration before expecting drift.
A1, R6 and AC27 require startup refusal before binding when no overlay path is derivable, and verify that an explicit overlay path permits startup.

new_findings.title: Status-file path can collide with configuration files
new_findings.evidence: A5 accepts --status-file PATH without excluding the base or managed overlay path, and R7 requires the launched runtime to replace that file with a status record; selecting either configuration path therefore destroys configuration and, for the base, contradicts R2's prohibition on writing it. R6 and AC27 only guard overlay-versus-base collisions. The specification is not sound enough to plan from until status-path collisions are addressed.

new_findings.title: Invalid status-record handling is unspecified
new_findings.evidence: R7 and AC32 define unknown for an absent record or dead pid, but specify no behavior for an unreadable, malformed or incomplete existing record at the operator-selected status path; AC34 only prevents partial records during compliant atomic publication.
